title: Two real players occupy two board rows each because name-variant drift splits one human across a resolved row and an unresolved ghost, stranding vendor votes
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md and src/identity/matcher.py:17-30 claim the position-aware canonical key prevents two rows for one player; validationSummary.duplicateCanonicalIdentityCount is the pinned detector.
observed: The live 1,092-row contract carries BOTH 'Matt Hibner' (playerId 13324, TE/BAL/24, rank 377, rankDerivedValue 1737, sourceCount 8) and 'Matthew Hibner' (playerId null, position null, same team BAL, same age 24) - the same human. The three source CSVs (ktc, ktcSfTep, idpTradeCalc) spell him 'Matthew Hibner', so their values 891/1458/1129 are stamped byte-identically on BOTH rows. dlfSf (rank 250.83), flockFantasySf (383.0) and draftSharks (400.0) land ONLY on the ghost, so the priced row blends 8 of 11 available vendor votes. Second case: 'Jam Miller' (playerId 13403, RB/NE, rank 635) vs 'Jamarion Miller' (playerId null) - DraftSharks' own CSV analysis text for 'Jamarion Miller' reads "Miller could make the Patriots roster as a third RB", identifying the same player; its rank-323 vote is stranded on the ghost. buildRows materializes both: /rankings renders 'Matt Hibner' at rank 377 AND 'Matthew Hibner' at rank 1052. validationSummary.duplicateCanonicalIdentityCount = 0 because that detector keys on exact _normalize_for_collision equality, and the split exists precisely because the keys differ.

reproduction.expected: 0 split identities; every human occupies exactly one board row
reproduction.actual: 1 CONFIRMED (Matthew/Matt Hibner, team+age identical, 3 byte-identical source values) + 1 REVIEW (Jamarion/Jam Miller); contract reports duplicateCanonicalIdentityCount=0

userImpact: A user searching /rankings for 'Hibner' sees the player twice - once at #377 with a value and once at #1052 without - and cannot tell which is real. The priced row's value is computed from 73% of the vendor votes the pipeline actually loaded for that player, so its rank is wrong by an unknown amount in the trade calculator, the finder and every engine that reads rankDerivedValue.

priorFinding.note: A24-F05 measured 0 name COLLISIONS in the pool builder and called the path inert. The live failure is the inverse class - a SPLIT, not a merge - which no prior finding names and which A24-F05's collision measurement structurally cannot see.

whatWorks: 0 duplicate playerIds and 0 duplicate position-aware canonical keys across all 1,092 rows; the position-aware key does prevent the Quay-Walker/Kenneth-Walker merge class it was built for.
rootCause: The merge key is a canonical NAME (Dynasty Scraper.py:4655 `entry = players_json.get(canonical, ...)`), and CANONICAL_NAME_ALIASES has entries for Kenneth->Kenny and Chig->Chigoziem but none for Matt<->Matthew or Jam<->Jamarion. The scraper's must_have_rookie_guarantee fallback then mints a second row for the unaliased spelling, and _enrich_from_source_csvs grafts CSV values onto whichever row matches each vendor's spelling.
requiredRepair: Deduplicate playersArray on sleeperId after enrichment, and add a near-name split detector (same surname + similarity >= 0.85 + exactly one side has no playerId) that raises a real flag instead of the hardcoded nearNameMismatchCount: 0. Alias-table additions treat symptoms, not the class.

title: Both identity-duplicate detectors on the contract are structurally unable to fire, and scripts/audit_identity.py renders a permanently empty section for the one that would have caught W06-F001
claimUnderTest: _validate_and_quarantine_rows docstring: 'Check 0: position-aware duplicate identity ... This is the entity-resolution duplicate the build-time assertion test will also surface.' scripts/audit_identity.py advertises 'Near-name value mismatches (same last name, different universes)' as report #6.
observed: Check 0 indexes on f"{_normalize_for_collision(name)}::{group}" - exact-key equality. A split identity has, by definition, two different keys, so the detector can never see it. The near-name rule that WOULD have seen it was retired: near_name_pairs is permanently [] and "nearNameMismatchCount": 0 is a literal at data_contract.py:3330. scripts/audit_identity.py reads validation['nearNameMismatches'] and prints '(none)'. Live output: NEAR-NAME VALUE MISMATCHES '(none)', CROSS-UNIVERSE NAME COLLISIONS '(none)', quarantined=1 (Brandon Knight, unsupported_position). An operator running the repo's own identity audit gets a clean bill on a board that demonstrably carries a split player.

reproduction.expected: the near-name section reports Matt/Matthew Hibner and Jam/Jamarion Miller

numericProof.formula: detector_hits = |{rows sharing an exact position-aware collision key}| + nearNameMismatchCount

userImpact: Nobody is told the board contains a duplicated player, so the wrong value in W06-F001 ships with a 'validated' stamp.

priorFinding.note: A12-F18 established nearNameMismatchCount is hardcoded 0 and the dead threshold constant. Confirmed, and extended: the retirement is what makes W06-F001 invisible, and scripts/audit_identity.py still advertises the retired check as report #6.

whatWorks: The quarantine pass itself runs on every build and does flag unsupported_position (Brandon Knight, T) and suspicious_disagreement (50 rows) with correct confidence degradation.
rootCause: The only surviving duplicate detector is exact-key; the fuzzy one was removed for false positives and replaced with a literal 0 rather than a tighter rule.
requiredRepair: Re-introduce a near-name detector scoped to (same surname AND >=0.85 similarity AND exactly one side lacks playerId) - that predicate produces 1 confirmed hit and 0 false positives on today's board, versus the 40+ the retired rule produced.

title: /api/player/{sleeper_id}/realized returns unmapped_player for every player because the Sleeper block never contains the key the identity mapper is handed
claimUnderTest: server.py:11260 'Find this player's GSIS via the unified mapper, then filter.' The route's own comment says the row-filter bug was the defect and was fixed.
observed: players_dir = sleeper_block.get("players") or sleeper_block.get("playerDict"). The Sleeper block the scraper writes (Dynasty Scraper.py:1297-1306) contains exactly leagueId, leagueName, teams, positions, playerIds, idToPlayer, scoringSettings, rosterPositions, leagueSettings - no 'players', no 'playerDict', ever. players_dir is therefore always None, _index_directory(None) returns four empty dicts, resolve_player returns None, and the route short-circuits at reason: unmapped_player. Confirmed live on four real Sleeper ids (A.J. Brown 5859, Josh Allen 4984, Bijan Robinson 9509, Kenny Gainwell 7567): all four return unmapped_player. The stats fetch SUCCEEDS first (the route would otherwise say no_stats_available), so the mapper is the sole blocker. /api/status corroborates: idMappingCoverage = {resolve_attempts: 8, unresolved: 8, coverage_pct: 0.0}. This is a key-name mismatch in committed code, not container state.

reproduction.command: for sid in 5859 4984 9509 7567; do curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt "http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/player/$sid/realized"; echo; done
reproduction.expected: weekly realized-points arrays for each player

numericProof.formula: resolvable = |{sid : sleeper_block['players'] is a dict and sid in it}|

userImpact: PlayerPopup's realized-points panel is empty for every player in every league. A user comparing a player's market value against his actual production sees nothing and concludes there is no data.

priorFinding.note: A22-F03 claims the route 'emits a full array of 0.0-point weeks'; A22-F02 claims IDP players 'silently return zero weeks'. Neither reproduces: the route never reaches the scoring stage for ANY player. Both describe behaviour downstream of a bail that always fires. Same for PRIOR-A21-F16's league-scoping claim - the response never contains weeks to mis-score.

whatWorks: The route's auth gate, flag gate, league resolution and the nfl_data weekly fetch all work - the fetch returns rows, which is why the response is unmapped_player rather than no_stats_available.
rootCause: server.py reads sleeper.players / sleeper.playerDict; the producer emits sleeper.playerIds (name->id) and sleeper.idToPlayer (id->name). No writer has ever produced the key the reader asks for.
requiredRepair: Either fetch the Sleeper player directory for the mapper, or resolve the GSIS id from idToPlayer[sid] plus the nflverse name index. A key rename alone is NOT enough - playerIds/idToPlayer carry no gsis_id.

title: config/identity/id_overrides.json cannot influence the board at all, and where it IS read the override loses to the directory it exists to override
claimUnderTest: unified_mapper docstring: 'UDFAs, practice-squad callups, and same-name-different-player cases live in config/identity/id_overrides.json - a flat map that short-circuits the match ladder.'
observed: Two separate failures. (1) SCOPE: neither Dynasty Scraper.py nor src/api/data_contract.py reads the file. Its only readers are unified_mapper.resolve_player (reachable solely from the always-failing /api/player/{id}/realized, see W06-F003) and src/playerctx/normalize.py. No override can affect a single value on the board. (2) PRECEDENCE: the override rung is step 2, AFTER the exact-sleeper_id rung at :275. Proven at runtime: with a directory containing sleeper_id 999 and an override for 999, resolve_player returns the DIRECTORY row (match_method='sleeper_id'); the override only fires when the directory has no such id. Since the documented use cases ('same-name-different-player', 'players with identical names across positions') are by definition players the Sleeper directory already knows, the override layer is unreachable for its stated purpose. src/playerctx/normalize.py:561-563 independently documents this from the other side. (3) The shipped file contains only _comment and _example_entry_only, and _example_entry_only is loaded as a live override key.

reproduction.actual: section B prints 'sleeper_id / DIRECTORY NAME / gsis 00-0000001'; live override keys = ['_example_entry_only']

numericProof.formula: board_rows_influenced_by_overrides = |{row : row.playerId set via an override}|

userImpact: An operator who edits id_overrides.json to fix a mis-identified player, redeploys, and re-scrapes sees no change on any board and gets no error - the documented remediation path for identity defects is inert.

priorFinding.note: A24-F04's secondary note observes the empty-map cache re-read. The precedence inversion (override loses to the directory) and the total absence of the file from the board path are new, and are proven at runtime here rather than by reading.

whatWorks: _load_overrides degrades correctly on a missing or malformed file (logs and returns {}), and reload_overrides behaves as documented.
rootCause: Ladder ordering: exact sleeper_id (step 1) is checked before the manual override (step 2), and no board-building module imports the loader at all.
requiredRepair: Move the override rung above the exact-id rung, and give the board path a real consumer - the natural one is Dynasty Scraper.py::_resolve_sleeper_identity, where every board playerId is actually assigned.

title: identityConfidence is a three-valued restatement of 'does this row have a playerId', that playerId was itself assigned by a name match, and no surface reads the field
claimUnderTest: _compute_identity_confidence documents a four-rung ladder (1.00 canonical_id / 0.95 position_source_aligned / 0.85 partial_evidence / 0.70 name_only) scoring 'how confident we are that this row represents the right entity'.
observed: Live distribution over 1,092 rows: 1.00 canonical_id x937, 0.95 position_source_aligned x144 (every pick, via the assetClass=='pick' short-circuit), 0.70 name_only x11. The 0.85 partial_evidence rung emits zero rows. The field is therefore a bijection with (playerId is not None, assetClass=='pick') - it adds no information. Worse, the 1.00 label is not earned: no source except pfkDynasty publishes a Sleeper id, and every playerId on the board comes from Dynasty Scraper.py::_resolve_sleeper_identity, a NAME lookup with a 0.90-threshold difflib fallback. Consumption: buildRows copies identityConfidence/identityMethod onto every row (dynasty-data.js:1151-1152, 1295-1296, 1782-1783), and a repo-wide grep across frontend/app, frontend/components and frontend/lib finds ZERO non-test readers. Only the sibling `quarantined` boolean is read (/rankings trust tile, /edge filters). Corroborating: the one quarantined row on today's board, Brandon Knight, is stamped identityConfidence 1.00.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json,collections; d=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W06/contract-full.json')); print(collections.Counter((r['identityConfidence'], r['identityMethod']) for r in d['playersArray']))"
reproduction.expected: a spread across four rungs reflecting match quality

numericProof.formula: identityConfidence == 1.00 iff playerId != null; == 0.95 iff assetClass=='pick'; else 0.70

userImpact: No direct user-facing number, but every downstream reader that treats 'identityConfidence 1.00' as evidence of a correct match is trusting a name join - including the Hibner row in W06-F001, which is stamped 1.00.

priorFinding.note: Independently reproduced A24-F02 and A12-F17 (identical 937/144/11 split, dead 0.85 rung). Extended in two ways they do not cover: the field has zero non-test consumers anywhere in the frontend, and the one row the quarantine pass flags is itself stamped 1.00.

whatWorks: identityMethod is internally consistent with identityConfidence, and the 11 name_only rows are genuinely the 11 rows with no Sleeper id.
rootCause: The score is computed from field presence rather than from the join that actually happened; the join method is never recorded on the row.
requiredRepair: Stamp the real join provenance from the enrichment cascade (sleeper_id / exact canonical name / alias-table / fuzzy) instead of re-deriving a score from playerId presence, then either render it or delete it.

title: unified_mapper.resolve_player merges 11 demonstrably different NFL players at its default threshold on today's real corpus, and the scraper's own fuzzy guard passes 5 of the same 11 pairs
claimUnderTest: Module docstring: 'Fuzzy normalized name only. confidence=0.75..0.90 ... Anything below the configured min_confidence is rejected.' _is_safe_name_merge: 'Guard fuzzy canonicalization so unrelated players are not merged.'
observed: Fed the 544 distinct source-CSV names that FAILED the production canonical-name join, plus a directory built from the live 948-player board, resolve_player(min_confidence=0.85) returns a match for 11 of them - every one a different human, each reported at confidence 0.857-0.923 with match_method='fuzzy_name' (a method the docstring caps at 0.90): Tevin Coleman->Kevin Coleman 0.923, Ian Thomas->Brian Thomas 0.909, Eric Gray->Cedric Gray 0.900, Ty Montgomery->Tyren Montgomery 0.897, Mike Williams->Mykel Williams 0.889, Cedrick Wilson->Eric Wilson 0.880, Jordan Travis->Jordan Davis 0.880, Jacob Harris->Jacob Parrish 0.880, Amari Cooper->Omar Cooper 0.870, Jordan Wilkins->Jordan Watkins 0.857. Separately, the ladder has no name+team rung: with two 'Josh Allen' rows (QB/BUF and LB/JAX) and no position supplied, resolve_player(name='Josh Allen', team='JAX') returns the BUF QB at confidence 1.00 - the caller's team is ignored entirely and the answer flips with dict insertion order. Blast radius is bounded by reachability: the live board join uses exact _canonical_match_key and correctly rejected all 544. But the scraper's OWN guard, _is_safe_name_merge, returns True for 5 of the 11 pairs (Tevin/Kevin Coleman, Ian/Brian Thomas, Eric/Cedric Gray, Cedrick Wilson/Eric Wilson, Cedrick Wilson Jr./Eric Wilson), and best_match is called at threshold 0.85 (line 4473) and 0.90 (4586, 5339) - so three of those pairs clear both the guard and the 0.90 gate on the live scrape path.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W06/repro_overrides_and_mapper.py  # sections C+D; full 11-pair sweep captured in fuzzy-false-merges.json
reproduction.expected: 0 matches among CSV names the exact join already rejected
reproduction.actual: 11 matches, confidence 0.857-0.923, all cross-player; and name+team resolution ignores team

numericProof.formula: false_merges = |{n : resolve_player(board_directory, name=n, min_confidence=0.85) is not None}| over names the exact canonical join rejected

userImpact: Not a live wrong number on the board today (the board join is exact). It is a loaded gun: any future caller that routes a source through resolve_player, and the scraper's own 0.85/0.90 fuzzy rungs, will attribute one player's value to another and report it above 0.85 confidence.

priorFinding.note: A24-F03 demonstrated the threshold problem on hand-picked name pairs. Confirmed and extended: measured against the 544 names the LIVE corpus actually fails to join (11 false merges), plus the new finding that Dynasty Scraper.py's _is_safe_name_merge guard admits 5 of those same pairs, so the defect is not confined to the unreachable module.

whatWorks: The exact-key production join (_canonical_match_key) rejected all 544 unmatched names with zero false merges - the conservative path is the one actually in use on the board.
rootCause: min_confidence is compared against a raw difflib ratio with no length, token or edit-position weighting; the fuzzy result overwrites confidence with that ratio; and there is no name+team rung between name+team+pos and name+pos.
requiredRepair: Require a surname exact match plus a first-name compatibility check before any fuzzy accept (the pool builder's _first_name_compatible already exists), add a name+team rung, and never report a fuzzy match above 0.90.

title: resolve_many rebuilds the entire Sleeper directory index once per input row - 203x its own documented cost
claimUnderTest: resolve_many docstring: 'Used by nightly jobs (injury feed, nflverse weekly ingest) so the mapper's internal index is built once, not per-row.'
observed: _index_directory sits inside resolve_player (:269), and resolve_many loops resolve_player. Measured on an 11,000-entry directory (Sleeper's real order of magnitude) with 200 inputs: 14.592s total vs 0.072s for a single index build - 199 redundant rebuilds, 99.5% of wall time. src/playerctx/normalize.py:551 documents the same problem and builds its own indexes to avoid it.
userImpact: No user-facing effect today (the batch path has no live caller), but any nightly job wired to it would take minutes instead of seconds.

priorFinding.note: Confirmed by direct timing rather than by reading; A24-F04 asserted the structure, this measures the 203x.

whatWorks: resolve_many's contract (returning unresolved rows verbatim) is honoured.
rootCause: Index construction is inside the per-row function.
requiredRepair: Hoist _index_directory into resolve_many and pass the prebuilt index down; keep resolve_player's single-row convenience wrapper.

title: Draft picks have no structured identity on the live path: season, round and slot exist only as substrings of a display name, re-parsed by at least nine divergent regexes, and the PickRow model that declares them is dead code
claimUnderTest: src/identity/models.py::PickRow declares season, round, slot_known, slot_number, bucket, league_id - the canonical pick identity. matcher.py branches on rec.asset_type == 'pick' to populate it.
observed: On the live contract's 144 pick rows, NONE of season / year / round / slot / originalOwner / currentOwner / projectedSlot exists as a field. playerId is null on all 144. The only identity is the displayName string ('2026 Pick 1.02', '2027 Early 1st'). Original and current owner do not exist in the contract at all - ownership lives only in sleeper.teams[].pickDetails and the draft-capital fallback. PickRow is unreachable on real data: src/adapters/scraper_bridge_adapter.py:101 hardcodes asset_type='player', so all 3,494 records in the newest raw snapshot are typed 'player' and matcher.py's pick branch never executes - /api/scaffold/identity reports pick_count 0 / pick_alias_count 0 while minting 84 master PLAYERS with ids like 'player::2026 early 1st::OTHER'. In place of the model, at least nine modules re-derive season/round/slot from the name with their own regexes, and they disagree: frontend/lib/pick-stack.js TIER_RE accepts rounds 1-9, data_contract._PICK_TIER_RE accepts 1-6; canonical/normalization_validator requires a two-digit slot (\.\d{2}) while _PICK_SLOT_RE accepts (0?[1-9]|1[0-2]); pool/builder caps the slot at 12.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json; d=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W06/contract-full.json')); p=[r for r in d['playersArray'] if r['assetClass']=='pick']; print(len(p)); print({k:sum(1 for x in p if x.get(k) is not None) for k in ['season','round','slot','originalOwner','currentOwner','projectedSlot','playerId']})" && curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/scaffold/identity | head -c 220
reproduction.expected: season/round/slot populated on all 144 picks; scaffold pick_count == 144

numericProof.formula: structured_pick_identity_coverage = fields_present / (144 rows x 5 canonical fields)

userImpact: Every surface that needs a pick's year, round or slot re-parses a display string, so a label the scraper emits in an unexpected shape (a 14-team slot, a one-digit slot, a round above 6) is silently classified as a PLAYER by some modules and a pick by others - the same asset then gets a player's treatment on one page and a pick's on another, with no error.

priorFinding.note: A24-F28 found one symptom (pool/builder's slot regex caps at 12). No prior finding states the underlying condition: there is no structured pick identity on the live path at all, and the model that declares one is unreachable because every raw record is typed 'player'.

whatWorks: pickAliases is internally consistent: all 18 generic->slot aliases (Early->x.02, Mid->x.06, Late->x.10) resolve to a slot row that carries a real rankDerivedValue, and every aliased generic row is correctly suppressed (rankDerivedValue null, pickGenericSuppressed true), so no double-count is possible on the 2026 class.
rootCause: The adapter that feeds the identity layer hardcodes asset_type='player', and the contract layer never promoted the parsed (year, round, slot) tuple from _PICK_SLOT_RE into row fields.
requiredRepair: Stamp season/round/slot (and slotKnown) onto every pick row in the contract once, from the parse the contract already performs, and have every consumer read those fields instead of re-parsing the name. Fixing asset_type in the bridge adapter is a prerequisite for the scaffold layer.

title: dynastyNerdsSfTep.csv ships a stable SleeperId column that the ID-join alias list cannot see, so a 294-row source joins by name only
claimUnderTest: data_contract.py:3570-3574: 'Optional Sleeper player-id column (today only pfkDynasty emits one). When present it gives ID-grade identity that survives vendor/Sleeper name-spelling drift.'
observed: dynastyNerdsSfTep.csv's header is Name,Rank,Value,SleeperId,Pos,Team - it emits one. _SLEEPER_ID_ALIASES = ('sleeper_id','sleeperId','sleeper_player_id') and _pick does an exact, case-sensitive dict lookup, so 'SleeperId' never matches. Measured: the parsed lookup for dynastyNerdsSfTep carries a sleeperId on 0 of 294 rows, versus 496 of 496 for pfkDynasty. Rescue value TODAY is zero (only 1 DynastyNerds row fails the name join - Dare Ogunbowale, who has no board row either), so this is latent, not live. The same measurement shows pfkDynasty's working ID join also rescues 0 rows today: 20 name misses, none corresponding to a board row. In other words, 100% of source->board joins on the live board are name joins.

reproduction.actual: dynastyNerdsSfTep 294 with sleeperId: 0 | pfkDynasty 496 with sleeperId: 496

userImpact: None today. Becomes real the moment DynastyNerds and Sleeper disagree on a spelling - that vendor's vote is then dropped from the blend with no warning, exactly the failure the pfkDynasty ID join was added to prevent.

priorFinding.note: Confirms docs/identity-audit-2026-07.md recommendation #1 as re-stated by A24-F26, and adds the measurement that neither ID join (Nerds or PFK) rescues a single row on the live board - every source->board join today is a name join.

whatWorks: pfkDynasty's sleeper_id column parses on 496/496 rows and the sid_index/audit-alias plumbing behaves as documented.
rootCause: Case-sensitive exact key lookup against a fixed alias tuple.
requiredRepair: Case-fold the header keys once when building each csvrow, or add 'SleeperId' to _SLEEPER_ID_ALIASES.

title: /api/scaffold/identity serves a 106-day-old identity report whose master players carry zero Sleeper IDs and whose pick table is empty, with no staleness marker on the response
claimUnderTest: CLAUDE.md lists GET /api/scaffold/identity as a live endpoint serving 'Identity mappings'.
observed: The endpoint returns 2.5 MB with generated_at 2026-04-20T19:48:28Z - 106 days before the live contract's 2026-08-04 - and the payload carries no age field. Contents: master_player_count 1788, player_alias_count 3494, pick_count 0, pick_alias_count 0, low_confidence_count 1906 (54.5% of aliases, ALL method 'exact_name_only'), and sleeper_id populated on 0 of 1788 master players because matcher.py:132 hardcodes sleeper_id="". 84 of the 1788 masters are draft picks minted as 'player::2026 early 1st::OTHER'. The producer scripts/identity_resolve.py is referenced by no workflow, timer or service, writes files named identity_resolution_*.json (zero exist on disk), and reads a raw snapshot whose newest file is also 2026-04-20. So the surface is a name-keyed master with no IDs, no picks, and no producer, served as current.

reproduction.command: curl -s -b /tmp/audit-cookies.txt http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/scaffold/identity | .venv/bin/python -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print({k:v for k,v in d.items() if not isinstance(v,list)}); print('sleeper_id populated:', sum(1 for p in d['players'] if p.get('sleeper_id')), 'of', len(d['players']))"
reproduction.expected: a report generated alongside the current contract, with sleeper_id populated and pick_count 144
reproduction.actual: generated_at 2026-04-20, pick_count 0, sleeper_id populated: 0 of 1788, low_confidence_count 1906

numericProof.formula: staleness_days = contract_date - report_date ; id_coverage = masters_with_sleeper_id / masters

userImpact: Any operator or integration reading /api/scaffold/identity to answer 'which player is this' gets a four-month-old, ID-free, pick-free answer presented as current.

priorFinding.note: Confirms A25-F10 / A23-F15 / A24-F23 on staleness and the missing producer. Extended with two measurements none of them make: sleeper_id is populated on 0 of 1788 masters (hardcoded empty at matcher.py:132) and pick_count is 0 because every raw record is typed 'player', so the whole PickRow branch is dead.

whatWorks: /api/scaffold/status DOES expose the file mtime, so the staleness is discoverable one endpoint away.
rootCause: matcher.py never resolves a Sleeper id, the bridge adapter never emits asset_type='pick', and no scheduler runs the producer.
requiredRepair: Either retire the endpoint or wire the producer to the refresh workflow and populate sleeper_id/asset_type. Whichever is chosen, stamp generated_at age on the response.

title: One rostered player is absent from the board and from all three Sleeper identity maps while still appearing on his team's roster lists
claimUnderTest: sleeper.playerIds / sleeper.idToPlayer / sleeper.positions are the identity maps for the league's rostered players.
observed: Team 'Ed' carries Sleeper id 7058 in both teams[].players (as 'Jaylinn Hawkins') and teams[].playerIds, but 7058 is absent from sleeper.idToPlayer, sleeper.playerIds and sleeper.positions (all 937 entries), and has no row in playersArray. Verified against the live Sleeper directory (read-only GET api.sleeper.app/v1/players/nfl): 7058 = Jaylinn Hawkins, SS/DB, BAL, status Active. fantasyProsIdp.csv ranks him 181, so at least one source prices him. He is therefore an owned asset with no value, no position and no id->name resolution on any surface. He is the only such case (1 of 666 rostered assets).

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json; d=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W06/contract-full.json')); s=d['sleeper']; b={str(r['playerId']) for r in d['playersArray'] if r.get('playerId')}; print([(t['name'],i) for t in s['teams'] for i in t['playerIds'] if str(i) not in b]); print('in idToPlayer:', '7058' in s['idToPlayer'])"

numericProof.formula: orphans = |{sid in any team.playerIds : sid not in idToPlayer}|

userImpact: Team Ed's roster value on /rosters and /league omits one IDP asset entirely, and no surface says a player was dropped.
whatWorks: The remaining 665 rostered assets round-trip name->id->name with zero failures, and playerIds/idToPlayer/positions are all exactly 937 entries with no name claimed by two ids.
rootCause: The identity maps are rebuilt from board rows after the blend (Dynasty Scraper.py:4837-4840), so a rostered player who never reaches the board is erased from the maps that ownership resolution reads.
requiredRepair: Seed the rebuilt maps from the roster pass rather than replacing them, so rostered-but-unpriced assets keep an id->name entry and can be rendered as 'owned, unpriced'.

title: The Sleeper name->id map is written with no collision guard while the sibling position map three lines above has one
claimUnderTest: The in-line comment at Dynasty Scraper.py:1238-1242 states the collision policy: 'Name collision across universes (e.g. DJ Turner WR vs DJ Turner II CB both clean to "DJ Turner"). Drop the entry entirely - having no position is safer than tagging the row with the wrong family.'
observed: That policy is applied to position_map only. Three lines earlier, player_id_map[cn] = sid and id_to_player[sid] = cn are written unconditionally on the same cleaned-name key. When two rostered players clean to one name, the second silently overwrites the first's Sleeper id in player_id_map, and id_to_player maps two ids onto one name - the exact asymmetry the comment argues against, on the exact example it names. Measured on the live block: 937/937/937 entries, 0 round-trip failures, 0 names claimed by more than one id - so the path is inert TODAY, and the position map's drop policy is doing the protective work by accident.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import json,collections; s=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W06/contract-full.json'))['sleeper']; print(len(s['playerIds']), len(s['idToPlayer']), len(s['positions'])); print('roundtrip failures:', sum(1 for n,i in s['playerIds'].items() if s['idToPlayer'].get(str(i))!=n)); print({k:v for k,v in collections.Counter(s['idToPlayer'].values()).items() if v>1})"
reproduction.expected: equal counts, 0 round-trip failures, {} - which is what happens today
reproduction.actual: 937 937 937 / 0 / {} - inert today, but unguarded by construction

numericProof.formula: len(playerIds) == len(idToPlayer) holds iff no two rostered players share a cleaned name

userImpact: None observed today. On the next roster that adds a name twin (the comment names DJ Turner WR vs DJ Turner II CB as a real case), one of the two loses his Sleeper id and inherits the other's ownership on every ID-first surface.

priorFinding.note: A24-F05 documents the same class in src/pool/builder.py. This is a second, independent instance in Dynasty Scraper.py that no prior finding names, and it sits three lines from a comment stating the correct policy for its sibling map.

whatWorks: position_map's collision policy is correct and does fire (the scraper prints a 'Dropped N colliding position entries' summary).
rootCause: The guard was added to one of three maps written in the same loop body.
requiredRepair: Apply the same drop-on-collision rule to player_id_map/id_to_player, or key all three on (cleanName, position) as src/identity/matcher.py already does.

title: Terminal re-derives each row's Sleeper ID by lowercased display name even though every row already carries playerId - verified correct on the live payload
claimUnderTest: terminal.py:191-196: 'The live pipeline emits playersArray WITHOUT _sleeperId on each row - that field only lives on the legacy players dict. When playersArray is populated we backfill each row with the _sleeperId from the matching dict entry.'
observed: Accurate about _sleeperId, but the rows DO carry the same value under playerId (data_contract.py:8790 maps _sleeperId -> playerId), and neither _players_array nor _build_sleeper_id_lookup looks at it - both key exclusively on lowercased displayName. Ran _players_array against the live full and app contracts: 1,092 rows, 937 _sleeperId recovered, 937 rows carrying playerId, and 0 rows where a playerId was present but the name join failed. The name join is correct today because both surfaces are minted from the same build and their display names are byte-identical. Recorded as verified, with the note that it is a name join standing in for an ID already on the row.

reproduction.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import sys,json;sys.path.insert(0,'.');from src.api import terminal as t;d=json.load(open('docs/master-site-audit/evidence/W06/contract-full.json'));r=t._players_array(d);print(len(r), sum(1 for x in r if x.get('_sleeperId')), sum(1 for x in r if x.get('playerId')), sum(1 for x in r if x.get('playerId') and not x.get('_sleeperId')))"

numericProof.formula: failures = |{row : row.playerId set and name-join produced no _sleeperId}|

priorFinding.note: Recorded as a verified negative: the name join works on the live payload.

whatWorks: Full 937/937 recovery on both the full and app views, with zero failures.
rootCause: The helper predates the playerId stamp and was never updated.
requiredRepair: Prefer row['playerId'] and keep the name join only as a fallback - a one-line change that removes a name join from a hot path.

title: Per-source name-join coverage measured on the live board: 17 of 21 sources join above 92%, but fantasyNavigatorSf loses 40% and draftSharksIdp 22% of their rows
claimUnderTest: The enrichment cascade's docstring claims exact -> alias-aware -> position-aware fallback resolves cross-source drift.
observed: Measured join rate per source against the live 1,092-key board: ktc 99.8%, ktcSfTep 99.8%, idpTradeCalc 99.9%, dlfIdp/idpShow/fantasyProsFitzmaurice/dlfRookieSf/dlfRookieIdp 100%, dlfSf 99.6%, dynastyNerdsSfTep 99.7%, otcffbSf 99.4%, dynastyDaddySf 99.5%, fantasyCalc 98.8%, fantasyProsIdp 96.8%, pfkDynasty 96.0%, flockFantasySf 94.8%, yahooBoone 92.0%, draftSharks 92.5%, flockFantasySfRookies 90.5%, fantasyProsSf 87.8%, draftSharksIdp 78.0%, fantasyNavigatorSf 60.0%. Independently reproduced by the repo's own scripts/audit_identity_matches.py to within 1 row on every source. Crucially, the misses are NOT identity failures: 455 distinct canonical keys appear in some CSV and in no board row at all, and spot checks (Maxwell Hairston, Benjamin Morrison, Christian Wilkins, Mason Rudolph, Tyrod Taylor, Odell Beckham) confirm those players have no board row under any spelling. The enrichment cascade only fills existing rows; it never creates one. 37 of the 455 are covered by 3 or more sources. Whether the pool should include them is a pool-construction question, not an identity one.

reproduction.expected: n/a - this is a measurement, not a claim under test
reproduction.actual: per-source rates as listed; 0 rows matched via the sleeper-id column on any source

numericProof.formula: join_rate(source) = |{csv canonical keys present in board}| / |{csv canonical keys}|

userImpact: None directly - a source row with no board row contributes nothing either way. Recorded so a later reader does not mistake the 40% fantasyNavigatorSf figure for an identity defect.

priorFinding.note: A24-F26 measured drift in docs/identity-audit-2026-07.md's per-source table. Re-measured independently on the live contract and reproduced the same figures (fantasyProsSf 87.8% vs the doc's 99.1%, flockFantasySfRookies 90.5%), and added the diagnosis A24-F26 does not make: the misses are absent-from-pool, not mis-joined.

whatWorks: POSITION_ALIASES (21 entries in src/utils/name_clean.py) covers every position token any live source emits (QB RB WR TE DE DT DL LB S CB DB) with no unmapped values, and canonical_position_group routes each to the right family.
requiredRepair: n/a. If the 37 multi-source absentees are wanted on the board, that is a pool-builder change, not an identity change.
